name: Georgia

sources.title: Georgia DOR -- 2025 Employer's Tax Guide (updated June 2025)
sources.quote: The income tax rate was reduced from a flat rate of 5.39% to a flat rate of 5.19%. Note: Employers must continue to withhold at the rate of 5.39% before the effective date of the change and can begin withholding at the new rate of 5.19% starting July 1, 2025. ... Georgia standard deductions have increased to $24,000 for taxpayers filing Married Filing Joint and $12,000 for Single, Head of Household, and Married Filing Separate taxpayers.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, ETA -- Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective January 2025

georgiaStatusDeduction.$comment: A genuine MID-YEAR change, not just a year-over-year one -- HB 463 cut the rate and raised the standard deduction/dependent allowance retroactively to 2026-01-01, but the EMPLOYER WITHHOLDING transition date is 2026-05-11 specifically (quoted directly from both the Governor's press release and the employer guide itself). Both tables verified against the guide's own worked examples for their respective periods. CORRECTED after an independent verification pass (2026-08-21): the higher MFJ standard deduction applies ONLY when one spouse works (G-4's own Status C). An employee who is MFJ with BOTH spouses working (G-4's Status B) gets the SAME lower deduction as Single/HoH/MFS -- confirmed independently via USDA NFC's own withholding bulletin (help.nfc.usda.gov/bulletins/2026/1784643404.htm), which uses its own S/M/N/H lettering but states the identical substance verbatim: code M = 'Married, Filing Joint Return (One Spouse Working)' = $30,000; code N = 'Married, Filing Separate Returns or Joint Return (Both Spouses Working)' = $15,000. The original version of this file only checked for a generic 'married_filing_joint' status with no one-vs-both-working distinction at all, which would have silently overpaid the $30,000 deduction to any MFJ-both-working employee.
georgiaStatusDeduction.statusCodesG4: Form G-4's own Line 3 letters: A=Single, B=Married Filing Separate OR Married Filing Joint (both spouses working), C=Married Filing Joint (one spouse working), D=Head of Household. ONLY C gets the higher standard deduction below -- engine reads certificate.georgiaMaritalStatus as one of these 4 letters, defaulting to the lower bucket (same as A/B/D) when absent, consistent with this project's 'absent certificate defaults to the least generous outcome' convention.

beforeMay11_2026.verifiedExample1: Same deductions as the July-2025 table; only the rate differs (5.39%).
beforeMay11_2026.verifiedExample2: See fromMay11_2026 examples; same deductions at 5.39%.

fromMay11_2026.verifiedExample1: 2025 guide (June 2025), Table E example: semimonthly $1,470.83, MFJ one spouse working, 1 dependent: 1,470.83 - 1,000.00 - 166.67 = 304.16 x 5.19% = 15.79.
fromMay11_2026.verifiedExample2: 2025 guide, Table F example: biweekly $730.77, HoH, 2 dependents: 730.77 - 461.54 - 307.70 = 0 -> $0.00.

georgiaStatusDeduction.formula: Annualize wages (periodWages x periodsPerYear). Subtract the standard deduction: the HIGHER figure ONLY for MFJ-one-spouse-working (Status C); every other status (A/B/D -- Single, HoH, MFS, MFJ-both-working) shares the SAME lower figure. If dependents are claimed, also subtract dependentAllowanceAnnual x count. Multiply the remainder (floored at $0) by the flat rate. Divide by periods. No whole-dollar rounding (cent precision throughout, confirmed by both worked examples' own cent-level answers).

exemptPretaxComment: Confirmed directly via the guide's own FAQ, the cleanest confirmation tier this project uses for this recurring question: 'Are contributions to qualified 401(k), profit sharing, or deferred compensation plans taxable? No.'

reciprocity.$comment: CHECKED, not assumed absent: the current 2026 guide (read in full) and Form G-4 both contain zero reciprocity language. Georgia has no bilateral reciprocity agreement with any state.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. Georgia statutorily preempts any city or county from levying a local income/wage tax -- confirmed structural, not just an observed absence, consistent with every source checked.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE. No mandatory or voluntary state-authorized paid family/medical leave program of any kind found for Georgia.

knownGaps: Descriptive notes carried from the 2026 file (reciprocity, local-tax rules, method comments) were checked against the 2025 source for the fields this engine computes from; narrative text that only describes 2026 history should be read as background.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset. The engine's key names (beforeMay11_2026 / fromMay11_2026) are the 2026 shape; for 2025 they hold the 5.39% table used through 2025-06-30 and the 5.19% table from 2025-07-01 (HB 111, retroactive to 2025-01-01 but withheld from July 1). Standard deductions $12,000 / $24,000 and the $4,000 dependent allowance applied all year.
